initial_requirements: State executive-branch agencies need a shared enterprise service for e-mail, messaging, calendars, and contacts. The service should support everyday communication and collaboration for agency users while allowing administrators to provision accounts, manage shared information, and apply organization-wide controls. The initiative is intended to meet confidentiality, privacy, security, retention, and operational needs while reducing the cost and duplication of separately supported agency systems.

messages.content: What are the most important outcomes this shared enterprise e-mail and collaboration service must achieve for the state agencies—for example, in terms of user productivity, administrative efficiency, security/compliance, cost reduction, and service consolidation?

The big outcome is that agency staff can communicate and collaborate reliably without each agency having to run its own separate system. We want users to have a consistent e-mail, calendar, and contacts experience that helps them do their day-to-day work faster and with fewer service problems.
From an administrative standpoint, the service should make account provisioning, shared management, retention, and policy enforcement much easier and more standardized. It also needs to improve security and compliance, especially around confidentiality, privacy, and record retention, while reducing duplicated systems and overall support costs across agencies.
